question: The 1857 revolt at Lucknow was led by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Begum Hazrat Mahal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Begum Hazrat Mahal** was one of the leading figures of the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
• She was the wife of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah, the ruler of Awadh (Oudh), whose kingdom was annexed by the British.
 
• After the annexation of Awadh, she took charge of the revolt at Lucknow and played a significant role in the uprising against the British East India Company.
 
• Begum Hazrat Mahal is remembered for her bravery and leadership in the struggle for independence and is considered a national hero in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1857 Revolt (Indian Rebellion of 1857)**

 
 
• The Indian Rebellion of 1857, also known as the First War of Indian Independence, was a major, but ultimately unsuccessful, uprising in India against the rule of the British East India Company.
 
• The revolt began on 10 May 1857 in the form of a mutiny of sepoys of the Company's army in the town of Meerut.
 
• It soon escalated into other mutinies and civilian rebellions, particularly in the upper Gangetic plain and central India.
 
• Significant leaders of the revolt included Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi, Tantia Tope, and Bahadur Shah Zafar in addition to Begum Hazrat Mahal.
 
 
 
• **Annexation of Awadh**
 
 
• Awadh (Oudh) was annexed by the British East India Company in 1856 under the pretext of misgovernance by Nawab Wajid Ali Shah.
 
• This annexation was part of Lord Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse, which aimed to annex Indian states with no clear heir or perceived misrule.
 
• The annexation of Awadh was one of the key events that led to widespread discontent and ultimately the 1857 revolt.
 
 
 
• **Nawab Wajid Ali Shah**
 
 
• Nawab Wajid Ali Shah was the last Nawab of Awadh (Oudh).
 
• He was known for his patronage of the arts, particularly music and dance.
 
• After the annexation of Awadh, he was exiled to Calcutta (Kolkata) by the British.
